item.title: Trent McDuffie proved worth in win over Packers
item.description: The defense led the Los Angeles Rams to a victory over the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night. Chris Shula’s unit forced three takeaways and allowed just 13 points to an opposing offense that can put up points in a hurry. One of the stronger individual performers? Trent McDuffie, one of LA’s prized offseason acquisitions. SumerSports charted 26 passing plays where McDuffie was matched up directly with a Packers receiver. You can’t realistically expect nor ask for better results. 11 plays vs Matthew Golden: 2 targets, 0 catches allowed 6 plays vs Christian Watson: 0 targets, 0 catches allowed 4 plays vs Tucker Kraft: 1 target, 0 catches allowed 3 plays vs Savion Williams: 1 target, 0 catches allowed 2 plays vs Bo Melton: 1 target, 1 catch for 12 yards While the Rams overall had trouble slowing down Watson, who accumulated four first-half receptions for 65 yards and a score before missing the second half due to injury, McDuffie was one of the defenders able to slow down his momentum. Kraft is one of the NFL’s top tight ends and the Rams held him to just three catches for 24 yards. Nate Landman punched out a fumble shortly after one of those receptions for a key defensive takeaway. All-in-all, Jordan Love finished with just 17 completions on 29 passes (59%) for 198 yards, one touchdown, two interceptions, and a passer rating of 62.1. This was an impressive outing for the Los Angeles defense. They limited Love and company even without the team’s other high-profile offseason addition at cornerback, Jaylen Watson. Emmanuel Forbes and Josh Wallace were also stingy in coverage, and that is a positive sign for the remainder of the season. Watson will not return in 2026. Even more positive is the fact the Packers had very little production on the ground. Savion Williams was the most efficient with two carries for 18 yards. Kaleb Johnson was held to 13 yards on eight carries (1.6 average). Byron Young and Myles Garrett each made notable tackles for loss that put Green Bay behind the chains. The Rams have now won five-straight games. Their previous four wins were against weaker competition. The defense is demonstrating they can get the job done even when facing superior quarterback talents and overall stronger opponents. Whether that is true for the offense remains to be seen. What is obvious is that the Rams are a defensive-led team in their current state. On Wednesday, Trent McDuffie proved his worth to a defense that is performing at a high level.

item.title: How Arsenal can expose Man City’s clear weakness to tighten grip on title
item.description: For Manchester City , life after three Champions League-winning midfielders began in earnest against Arsenal in August. They were a goal down after 23 seconds. It was an inauspicious start for Enzo Maresca and Elliot Anderson alike. A reunion with Arsenal on Sunday could be deemed a meeting of managerial midfielders, in Maresca and Mikel Arteta . Each learned from Pep Guardiola , who won the European Cup as a Barcelona player and manager and then in charge of City. But it is also a first Premier League clash since Bernardo Silva and Rodri joined their mentor in decamping from the Etihad Stadium in the summer. Arsenal may not have been sorry to see any go; if Guardiola’s resignation could facilitate an era of dominance from Arteta, and if it may have already begun with last season’s Premier League title, a further factor could be the departures of the City captain and Spain’s World Cup-winning skipper. If City have been confronted with the question of how to replace the irreplaceable, there are different answers. One is simply that it is impossible: they are irreplaceable. Another is: expensively. City committed £326m to three midfield recruits, in Anderson, Ayyoub Bouaddi and Enzo Fernandez . A third is: incoherently, at least so far. Perhaps it is unfair to expect newcomers, both in the dugout and the centre of the pitch, to bring the same cohesion and chemistry as predecessors who became the faces of longevity and continuity, but thus far they have not. A further subplot, arguably, is that Arsenal boast men who represented an alternative line of succession at City: not merely Arteta, Guardiola’s first assistant in Manchester, but Bruno Guimaraes , who was of interest at the Etihad in 2024, but when City chose not to activate his release clause, and Declan Rice , the target who preferred to join Arsenal in 2023. Arguably the England vice-captain was the best central midfielder in the Premier League even with Rodri and Silva; without them, and despite Pascal Gross’ extraordinary start to the season, he definitely is. item.title: Adeyemi, Gavi react after Sabah 1-4 Barcelona: ‘We want to win every match’
item.description: Adeyemi, Gavi react after Sabah 1-4 Barcelona: ‘We want to win every match’ Karim Adeyemi continued his impressive UEFA Champions League form as Barcelona defeated Sabah 4-1 in Baku, while Gavi used the opportunity to underline his importance to Hansi Flick’s squad despite limited playing time this season. Adeyemi replaced the absent Lamine Yamal and delivered another influential performance, scoring after a superb assist from Alejandro Balde. The German forward has now scored in three of Barcelona’s five Champions League matches, strengthening his case as an important attacking option during the club’s demanding schedule. Adeyemi makes the most of Lamine Yamal’s absence Adeyemi’s goal was a positive contribution after Flick trusted him to cover for Yamal, and after the match, the forward said he was pleased to help Barcelona secure the three points. “The goal means a lot to me; I’m pleased for the team that I was able to help secure the win, and we can be happy with the three points,” he began. The German also recognised the challenge of playing away from home and praised Anthony Gordon, who scored twice against Sabah. “It’s always difficult to play away from home; they did a great job and were very motivated. Gordon? He had a very good game; I’m happy for the team and for him, and I hope he keeps scoring more goals.” Karim Adeyemi scored from Alejandro Balde’s assist. (Picture credit: X/@FCBarcelona) Adeyemi then insisted Barcelona have enough quality to cope without their teenage star. “He’s an important player and we have the quality to replace him. At Barça, there must always be replacements, regardless of the position. “We mustn’t rely on anyone or be afraid of anyone. We’re here to win and we want to win every match.” Gavi insists he remains important despite reduced minutes Gavi made his third start of the season against Sabah and played 86 minutes, offering Flick another opportunity to assess the midfielder’s readiness for a greater role. The Spain international acknowledged his importance within the squad while recognising that every player must understand their responsibilities. “Every player is important and everyone needs to be clear about their role. I consider myself important even though I’m not getting as many minutes at the moment, and I must always contribute to the team,” Gavi emphasised. item.title: Scott Gardner proud of the performance despite Fleetwood defeat
item.description: Scott Gardner proud of the performance despite Fleetwood defeat Leeds United Under-21s saw their Jersey Mike's Trophy campaign end in the group stages, after a defeat away at Fleetwood Town on Wednesday evening. The Sky Bet League Two side secured the three points they needed to progress into the knock-out stages, in a game that was all to play for. Scott Gardner's young side had put themselves in with a chance of qualification, but needed a result on the night at the Highbury Stadium, which ultimately they did not get. Speaking after the game, Gardner reflected on a spirited performance from his team. He said: "I thought we were very good and I thought we deserved something from the game. “We looked much more like ourselves tonight compared to the Oldham game and we had enough moments to win it. “But, you know, those moments are key, so if you don't take your chances, senior players find a way. They got two goals in the last 10 minutes, it's a shame for the players, but there’s loads we can take from it. “We knew that there was a respect from them [Fleetwood] and obviously a desire to go through. But our players showed they're more than capable across the board, and hopefully people can see that and the effort they put in. “I'm really proud of this group and how they work every day and wanted to get through, but we have to go again. I am disappointed for them they haven't got the reward of going through, but, you know, credit for how they performed.”

item.title: Knee surgery rules Sinner out of Australian Open
item.description: Jannik Sinner is a five-time Grand Slam champion [Getty Images] Jannik Sinner has been ruled out of the Australian Open in January following an operation on his knee. The 25-year-old Italian, who won the 2024 and 2025 titles at Melbourne Park, has not played competitively since winning Wimbledon on 12 July. In a social media post on Tuesday, world number two Sinner said he had undergone surgery to "improve the condition of my iliotibial band" - a thick band of tissue that runs along the outside of the knee. "We've been in regular touch with Jannik's team and they've confirmed he won't be joining us for the AO [Australian Open] in January following his recent surgery," said Tennis Australia chief executive Andrew Abdo. "Jannik loves competing here in Melbourne and is looking forward to returning for AO 2028. We wish him all the very best with his recovery and look forward to seeing him back on court soon." The 2027 Australian Open main draw starts on 17 January. Sinner's challenge at the 2026 tournament was ended by a five-set semi-final defeat by Novak Djokovic. Sinner was the dominant player for the first half of the season, winning 44 and losing just three of his singles matches. He won five Masters 1000 titles in a row between March and May, becoming the youngest man to complete the 'career Golden Masters', and reclaimed the world's top ranking from Alcaraz along the way. However, he suffered a shock second-round exit at the French Open, with Zverev ultimately stepping up to win his first Grand Slam title. Sinner bounced back on the grass courts, demolishing Novak Djokovic in the semi-finals before coming back from a set down against Zverev in the Wimbledon showpiece. He ended his season in early October, meaning he was unable to defend the points he claimed with title triumphs in China, Vienna, Paris and the ATP Finals at the end of 2025. Zverev went on to win the US Open and secure the year-end number one ranking. item.title: Lions’ late owner Martha Firestone Ford will be on Matthew Stafford’s mind as he watches ex-team play on Thanksgiving
item.description: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford talks with former Detroit Lions owner Martha Firestone Ford. For years, Thanksgiving in the Stafford household meant watching Dad play quarterback for the Detroit Lions. Even after Matthew Stafford joined the Rams, his wife and daughters still had to share him with football. At some point every Turkey Day, he was due at practice. That was Thanksgiving for Stafford. He was either playing in a game or preparing for one. Matthew Stafford throws a pass during the Rams’ 26-13 win over the Packers on Nov. 25, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, Calif. Getty Images This year, the Rams got their work done Wednesday night against the Packers in the NFL’s inaugural Thanksgiving Eve game. For the first time in as long as he can remember, Stafford gets the whole day with his family. And when the Lions come on, his wife and daughters can slide over and make room for Dad on the couch. “I’ll be tuning in just like everybody else,” Stafford said. Except there’s someone he’ll be thinking about when his old team takes the field. Martha Firestone Ford, the Lions’ owner and chair emeritus, died this week . And for all the pleasure Stafford takes in the prospect of a Thanksgiving at home, he said he’ll be “a little heavy-hearted” watching the Lions play. He was a kid from Texas by way of the University of Georgia when the Lions made him the first pick in the 2009 NFL draft. Ford had been part of the organization since 1963, when she and her husband, William Clay Ford, purchased the team. By the time Stafford came along, she had spent nearly half a century welcoming people to Detroit. Detroit owner Martha Firestone Ford, who died this week, plays with Sawyer Stafford, held by her mother Kelly Stafford, before a home game against the Falcons. USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect He remembers how warmly she welcomed him and his family. “She’s a special lady to me, to my family, and to that organization to the city of Detroit,” Stafford said. He spent his first 12 NFL seasons there. Along the way, he got to see another side of the woman who had made him feel at home. When her husband died in 2014, Ford took over the Lions herself. The relationship Stafford built with Ford has made her passing all the more painful. Even as he prepared to play the Packers, his heart was with his second family in Detroit. “I’ve reached out to them a little bit,” Stafford said. “Just an unbelievable lady, a great leader, and she’ll be missed.” Even after the trade to Los Angeles, Thursdays in November generally meant practice for the next opponent. It took the NFL putting the Rams and Packers in its inaugural Thanksgiving Eve game Wednesday to give Stafford the first full Thanksgiving off he can remember in years. item.title: Spurs Fall To Trail Blazers In NBA Cup Despite Wemby’s Monster Game: 4 Things We Learned
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Jaime Valdez-Imagn Images Victor Wembanyama did everything he could to carry the San Antonio Spurs to an NBA Cup victory, but it wasn’t enough to overcome the Portland Trail Blazers . Despite a monster 44-point, 16-rebound performance from their superstar, the Spurs fell 116-111 in a game decided by Portland’s efficiency on both ends. Wembanyama was spectacular, shooting 17-30 from the field and adding two blocks while playing 35 minutes. Devin Vassell added 18 points, and Stephon Castle finished with 20 points and nine assists. But San Antonio struggled to find consistency from beyond the arc, connecting on just 10-36 three-point attempts. Just an ugly shooting night. Portland had their own stars show up. Deni Avdija erupted for 33 points, 12 rebounds, and seven assists, while Damian Lillard added 29 points and seven assists. The Trail Blazers also received 16 points from Sidy Cissoko and 11 from Jrue Holiday off the bench. Here are four things we learned from San Antonio’s disappointing NBA Cup loss. 1. Victor Wembanyama Is Nearly Impossible To Stop Wembanyama had an extraordinary performance, and the numbers barely do justice to how much San Antonio relied on him. The Spurs superstar finished with 44 points and 16 rebounds on 17-30 shooting. He also knocked down three three-pointers, converted seven free throws, and recorded two blocks. Portland had no reliable answer for him individually. Wembanyama found easy ways to score and looked like the best player in the world tonight. He also finished with a +2 rating despite San Antonio losing by five points. That is particularly telling when considering how much the Spurs struggled to generate offense outside their primary contributors. The frustrating part for San Antonio is that a 44-point, 16-rebound performance from Wembanyama should normally put a team in an excellent position to win. Instead, the Spurs wasted one of his best performances by failing to provide enough shooting around him. 2. Deni Avdija And Damian Lillard Were A Dynamic Offensive Duo Portland’s victory was built around two outstanding performances from Avdija and Lillard. Avdija was arguably the most complete player on the floor outside Wembanyama, finishing with 33 points, 12 rebounds, and seven assists. He shot 11-21 from the field and 5-8 from three-point range, giving the Spurs problems from virtually every area of the court. Lillard provided another major scoring threat, recording 29 points and seven assists. Although he shot just 7-20 overall, he made five three-pointers and converted all 10 of his free-throw attempts. Together, they combined for 62 points and 14 assists. That production gave Portland enough offensive firepower to withstand Wembanyama’s monster night. Ever since Nathan MacKinnon was injured , which came moments after Cale Makar ‘s injury, the Avs have seemingly tightened up their game. Maybe they were overly reliant on their superstars and needed to get a little uncomfortable. Or maybe it’s what Jared Bednar talked about weeks ago, that veteran teams sometimes need a little time to get going. Either way, something is working. The Avalanche got Makar back against the Montreal Canadiens on Wednesday and went on to complete a 6-0 rout of one of the best teams in the Eastern Conference. Makar wasn’t the biggest difference-maker in this one. It wasn’t even Mackenzie Blackwood , who helped the Avs record their third consecutive shutout win on home ice by making 27 saves. It was Devon Toews . The Avalanche’s veteran defenseman has been magnificent this season and continued that trend against the Canadiens. Toews scored two of Colorado’s six goals. He also played 22:59, including 4:50 on the power play. One of his goals came on the man advantage where he’s currently quarterbacking the top unit. item.title: Maxx Crosby sends clear message on Deshaun Watson ahead of Browns showdown
item.description: Credit: Mitchell Leff/Jared C. Tilton via Getty Images Maxx Crosby has made his feelings clear on Deshaun Watson ahead of the Las Vegas Raiders’ clash with the Cleveland Browns, describing the quarterback as a major threat. The Raiders are preparing for their first primetime appearance of the season, with their defence facing the challenge of containing Watson and his ability to make plays both through the air and on the ground. Watson impressed in his previous outing against the Houston Texans, completing 25 of 40 passes for 312 yards while adding 49 rushing yards and a touchdown on eight carries. Maxx Crosby explains why Deshaun Watson poses a major threat Crosby knows the Raiders will need to be at their best to limit the Browns quarterback, who has shown he can create problems even when a play breaks down. Speaking to reporters , the Las Vegas defensive star praised Watson’s physical attributes and ability to lead Cleveland’s offence. “[Watson is] a dual-threat guy,” Crosby said. “He’s had a lot of success in this league. He’s got a really strong arm, tough, mobile, and can make a lot of off-schedule plays. He can obviously process as well. “He’s a really good quarterback [and] is leading those guys, and I’ve got a lot of respect for his game. We know it’s another challenge. He’s a really good guy, and for us, we’ve got to be at our best to slow him down and mess up his day.” Crosby also admitted the Raiders are excited about playing under the primetime spotlight, although he knows the pressure is on his team to deliver. “We’re fired up,” he added. “It’s awesome. You want to play on the biggest stages against the best team.” The defensive end described the situation as “do or die” for Las Vegas, with the team desperate to secure a significant win before its bye week. Meanwhile, former Browns player Hanford Dixon believes Cleveland should win the matchup but admitted he has concerns about Raiders quarterback Fernando Mendoza. Dixon suggested the rookie has started to look more comfortable in the pocket and is beginning to understand the demands of the position. That gives Cleveland another challenge to consider, even with Crosby making it clear that stopping Watson will be a major priority for the Raiders. Mandatory Credit: Jaime Valdez-Imagn Images The Portland Trail Blazers (12-6) have earned the reputation of a dark horse in the West this season. While this may be true, their 116-111 victory against the San Antonio Spurs in Wednesday night’s NBA Cup matchup should see them rated as a genuine threat in the West. The Trail Blazers looked dominant against the Spurs. Although the game was neck-and-neck for the most part, Portland’s tenacity and unwillingness to give up eventually broke down San Antonio’s defense, as they outscored the Spurs 32-24 in the fourth quarter to secure the win. Portland’s winning effort was led by the pair of Deni Avdija and Damian Lillard , who combined for a whopping 62 points. Aside from them, the late-game contributions of Jrue Holiday and the scoring boost by Scoot Henderson played a vital role in sealing the deal. The Spurs also had some standout performers, with Victor Wembanyama (44 PTS, 16 REB, 2 BLK) and Stephon Castle (20 PTS, 6 REB, 9 AST) outscoring the Blazers’ duo with a combined 64 points. Unfortunately, with solid contributions across the board, Portland would not be denied this win. Along with his monster 33-point performance to pave the way for Portland, Avdija played some solid defense and placed an incredible amount of pressure on San Antonio’s wings. item.description: Barcelona's Brazilian forward #09 Gabriel Jesus reacts during the UEFA Champions League match between Sabah and Barcelona at the Baku Olympic Stadium in Baku on November 25, 2026. (Photo by Igor IVANKO / AFP via Getty Images) | AFP via Getty Images Gabriel Jesus was happy with his goal but not his performance in Barcelona’s 4-1 win over Sabah in the Champions League on Wednesday. The summer signing was in the starting XI for the match as Hansi Flick rotated his side and did get on his scoresheet. Speaking afterwards, Jesus explained why he had found it tough going in Baku against Sabah. “It’s always difficult, the Champions League is. Obviously, everyone can talk about Barça, but if Sabah is in the competition, it’s because they have a good team. We have played some players who haven’t participated as much in recent matches. We have won, I’m happy about the goal but not so much about my performance. Happy, but I hope I can keep helping the team,” he told reporters. “Normally, when players who haven’t been playing as much, it’s hard to find the rhythm, and at the start of the match I think it showed. This is part of the game.” Jesus admitted he’s well aware that he’s a squad player but he’s still hoping for more minutes as the season progresses. “We are here to help Barça become a better team. I understand my situation and try to stay in shape. Training without playing is complicated, but that’s how it is. We try to help, the decision is Flick’s. Scoring goals is always good,” he added. “The goal is very important. I always want to score goals. My role is different. Rapha is scoring a lot and is very important to us. item.title: Navajo Stirling & Carlos Ulberg Make Decision on Future UFC Fight
item.description: Navajo Stirling Carlos Ulberg UFC Getty UFC light heavyweight teammates Navajo Stirling and Carlos Ulberg have made a decision about a future fight against each other. Ulberg is the current UFC light heavyweight champion, while Stirling is one of the top contenders in the weight class following his KO win over Jiri Prochazka at UFC Qatar — the same man whom Ulberg beat to collect the title back in April at UFC 327. These two men should fight for the belt next. But with both fighters training at City Kickboxing in Auckland, New Zealand, it makes things a bit more difficult. Now, we know what their decision is. Navajo Stirling Won’t Fight Carlos Ulberg According to CKB head coach Eugene Bareman , the team has decided that Stirling will not fight Ulberg, even if the belt is on the line. “Boys from the same gym don’t fight. We’ve had this agreement from the very beginning of the gym. Some things are bigger than fighting. Friendship and the bond you’ve built with someone are bigger than fighting,” Bareman said. 🚨🏆Eugene Bareman confirms Carlos Ulberg and Navajo Stirling will NOT fight each other for the title: “Boys from the same gym don't fight. We've had this agreement from the very beginning of the gym. Some things are bigger than fighting. Friendship and the bond you've built… pic.twitter.com/Hrzfbr8lwi — Home of Fight (@Home_of_Fight) November 26, 2026 Team Holding Navajo Stirling Back Based on this decision, it seems like Stirling is being held back from doing what he set out to do when he first became an MMA fighter, which is to win the UFC title. There is no doubt that this is a difficult situation for the team and for both fighters involved, because MMA is partly a team sport. But it’s also an individual sport, and the team choosing for these two not to fight each other is holding Stirling back from testing himself against the champ. For Ulberg, this is an easier decision, because as the champion he has other contenders whom he can fight, such as Magomed Ankalaev. But for Stirling, the decision not to fight his teammate is one that could change the trajectory of his entire career. It will be interesting to hear what UFC president Dana White has to say about this, because he’s always said in the past that MMA fighters need to look out for themselves, and in this case, it looks like the team is putting Ulberg first. Nothing highlights that quite like what unfolded at the turn of the year when clubs in Europe were circling as her contract with the Washington Spirit expired. Desperate not to lose one of the most talented and recognisable players in the league, the NWSL introduced its High Impact Player rule, quickly nicknamed ‘the Rodman rule’, in order to allow the Spirit to offer Rodman the sort of contract that could keep her around, making her the highest-paid women’s footballer in the world . How Rodman performed in the season that unfolded afterwards only served to justify the deal. A return of 14 goals and 10 assists helped fire the Spirit into the 2026 NWSL Championship game, in which she also scored despite her side’s eventual defeat . item.title: “Hasn’t really recovered”: Peter Schmeichel pinpoints where it has all gone wrong for Senne Lammens at Man United
item.description: “Hasn’t really recovered”: Peter Schmeichel pinpoints where it has all gone wrong for Senne Lammens at Man United Manchester United goalkeeper Senne Lammens had a disastrous evening for the club in their 2-2 draw with Sporting CP. Story of the match The Red Devils made another poor start in Europe, conceding the first goal for the fourth European match in a row. Lammens had actually been the hero moments earlier when he had managed to save Luis Suarez’s penalty but was the villain of the piece just seconds later. The Belgian came charging out of his goal and brought down the Sporting attacker, giving the referee an easy call to make. United then recovered in the second half and fought their way back to a 2-1 lead thanks to two goals from former Sporting hero Bruno Fernandes. Mauricio Pochettino’s side looked like they were destined to hold on and win just their fourth match of the season but they once again got in their own way. Lammens, who was so reliable last year, once again managed to ruin the night when he dropped a cross under very little pressure and Suarez tucked away the rebound in acrobatic style. Peter Schmeichel’s take The Champions League-winning goalkeeper who played for both clubs suggested he was worried that Lammens has not recovered from his disastrous cameo from the bench which cost Belgium in their World Cup defeat to Spain in the summer. Speaking to CBS Sports (via The Sun ), he explained that he doesn’t think taking Lammens out of the team would have any real benefit. He explained, “yeah, I don’t know when that point is. Pochettino has come in, he’s brought his own staff, that means he’s got a new goalkeeping coach. Maybe that is something that can change it for him.” The Dane continued to state, “in the World Cup he came on against Spain and made a mistake. Merino scored and they got knocked out and I feel like he’s lost confidence from that mistake, hasn’t really recovered. As a goalkeeper, when you’re not on your best form you need your defenders in front of you to help you out and they haven’t been able to do that and that just makes it so much worse and today was not a great day for him.” Lammens will likely have a chance to make amends when United welcome Brentford to Old Trafford on Saturday afternoon in Pochettino’s Old Trafford debut. item.title: ‘Am I crazy?’ – Bill Simmons thinks the Packers have been ‘screwed’ by NFL referees in 2026
item.description: Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images Bill Simmons has publicly brought up one of the major concerns he’s observed about how NFL officials have been treating the Green Bay Packers in the 2026 NFL season. The Packers fell to a 26-13 loss to the Los Angeles Rams on November 25 for Wednesday Night Football. While it was hard to overcome Blake Corum’s 200+-yard rushing performance, Packers fans left the game feeling hard-done by the referees once again. It was a pattern that multiple online fans have been bringing up for weeks that became more apparent after the loss to the Rams. It’s gotten to the point where even Bill Simmons feels like it merits a discussion. Bill Simmons questions if Packers are the worst officiated NFL team in 2026 After the Packers loss to the Rams, veteran media personality Bill Simmons shared a message on X, questioning if his eyes telling him that the Packers are consistently getting screwed is real or not. “Have the Packers gotten screwed by more calls than every other team in 2026 or am I crazy?” There is some truth to Simmons assertion, with specific areas of foul-calling seeing an almost historic swing against the Packers. The Packers have been the most penalised team in the NFL when it comes to roughing the passer, with another controversial call in this regard made against the Rams. The nine roughing-the-passer calls against the Packers are the most in the NFL by more than double, with the second-ranked team picking up four roughing-the-passer calls over the season. Not only that, Packers QB Jordan Love has drawn zero roughing flags this season despite being hit frequently by opposing defenders throughout the season. The disproportionate ‘roughing the passer’ calls for and against the Packers have become too much to ignore. The Packers also rank near the bottom for unnecessary roughness and personal fouls this season. Outside of these specific areas, the Packers have not seen any patterns that break the league’s overall average. Teams like the Carolina Panthers and Cleveland Browns rank higher in terms of the absolute most-penalised teams in the NFL, but the debatable nature of what’s happening in Packers games and the lack of proportion in ‘roughing the passer’ is raising more eyebrows. item.description: Blake Corum spent his 26th birthday handing out punishment instead of opening presents. The Los Angeles Rams running back bulldozed his way through the Green Bay Packers for a career-high 184 rushing yards on 32 carries in Wednesday night’s 26-13 Thanksgiving Eve victory at SoFi Stadium. Not only were Corum’s 32 carries the most by any NFL running back this season, but they were also the most by a Rams running back in more than a decade. Blake Corum now up to 184 yards rushing pic.twitter.com/xOJ3Oa2ejO — NFL (@NFL) November 26, 2026 Todd Gurley was the last Rams running back to eclipse the 30-carry threshold, rushing 30 times for 159 yards on Oct. 11, 2015, ironically against the same Packers franchise. Perhaps the most remarkable part of Corum’s accomplishment? He’s not even the Rams’ starting running back. That distinction still belongs to Kyren Williams, although the workload suggests the lines between starter and backup are becoming increasingly blurred. During the Rams’ five-game winning streak, Corum has amassed 508 rushing yards on 88 carries compared to Williams’ 71 attempts. item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. item.description: Cavan Sullivan named MLS Young Player of the Year 🌟 Philadelphia Union and USMNT midfielder Cavan Sullivan has capped a record-setting regular season by being named the 2026 MLS Young Player of the Year. item.title: How Columbus Crew turned it all around to set up MLS playoff showdown vs. Messi
item.description: It wasn’t working. Issa Tall had to admit that. Well, he didn’t really have to. The results told the story for him. The Columbus Crew didn’t win in its first five MLS matches. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Gotham FC’s title defense comes to crushing end in semifinal loss after venue change
item.description: They came by car, by the special-event X80 bus, by bike if they were feeling sporty. They came in layers, in beanies and scarves, with Gotham’s black-and-sky-blue colors on top. They came on behalf of those who couldn’t come, capacity being reduced at this impromptu change of venue, each one trying to make noise for five. Gotham FC forward Sam Kerr (20) competes for the ball against Kansas City Current defender Gabrielle Robinson (24) on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, in New York City. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect They came with some measure of outrage — these home-field shenanigans would never happen in men’s sports — while their better angels told them to come in joy, in celebration, everyone watching women’s sports. And then, 25 miles and 20,000 seats removed from their regular destination at New Jersey’s Sports Illustrated Stadium, huddled in the bleachers by a blue track ringing an immaculate pitch at Icahn Stadium on Randall’s Island, in the shadow of the old Psychiatric Center and with the light fading over the Costco across the river, 5,000 devoted souls Sunday afternoon watched Gotham’s NWSL title defense end in a 2-1 semifinal loss to the Kansas City Current. “We lost today because we weren’t the better team,” Gotham winger and oracle Midge Purce said. “That being said, I would say it’s inexcusable. It’s not what you want in a professional league. It’s not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it’s a bad look for everyone involved. And we always want to be at Sports Illustrated in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season. But I would say it had no effect on performance today.” The match had been moved to Icahn on Monday due to concerns over the disintegrating field conditions at Sports Illustrated, which had unfortunately overshadowed Gotham’s quarterfinal victory there last weekend. Gotham was unbeaten in its past 13 matches at Sports Illustrated, which is operated by the Red Bulls of MLS. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram. item.title: Messi makes history with MLS Golden Boot
item.description: Messi retired from international football with Argentina earlier this year [Getty Images] Inter Miami forward Lionel Messi has become the first player in MLS history to win the Golden Boot in consecutive seasons. The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner scored 26 goals in 31 appearances, four clear of FC Dallas striker Peter Musa and five more than Nashville's English forward Sam Surridge. Messi becomes only the sixth player to land the award twice, joining a list that includes former Charlton Athletic and Southampton striker Bradley Wright-Phillips. In addition to his goals, the 39-year-old notched 17 assists over the course of the MLS season, ensuring his 43 goal contributions was also a league best for the second year in a row. And the World Cup winner could soon make more history as he bids to become the first three-time Landon Donovan MLS MVP winner. The former Argentina forward landed the award in 2024 as Inter Miami won the Supporters' Shield title and also in 2025 as they won the MLS Cup. Despite Messi's magic, Miami weren't able to land top spot in the MLS Eastern Conference, with the team finishing 17 points behind Surridge's Nashville. They will now face Columbus Crew over three games in the first round of the MLS Cup play-offs which begin later this month.
